Question: What do I do for high school? Everything seems so boring/hard and I'm currently in 8th grade. How do I not fail all my classes and just do better?
Answer: You are beginning to learn a valuable lesson about maturity and taking on adult responsibilities. All adults will tell you that life and career involves accepting tasks that you find less than pleasant because the outcome is going to be worth the effort. Learning is not easy, and the work that you need to do to learn is not necessarily always interesting or engaging. Are you an athlete? Or a musician? If you are, you know that you never reach your goals without a great deal of regular practice. It is not easy, and it can be extremely boring repeating exercises over and over until they are perfect, but people in athletics and music keep their eyes on the prize and are willing to work with the knowledge that the work will pay off in terms of progress, which will be eventually rewarded. Successful adults know this very well. Ask your parents what they ever had to do that was hard and even boring, but eventually resulted in success. I know they will have many stories from their own lives, and you will be very gratified hearing them. In high school and later in college, the hard work you must do is to have a regular study schedule every day. Study should be 25% review, 50% focused on current lessons and 25% looking ahead to the next material. Once you establish this routine, it will become something that you will simply do every day like brushing your teeth. And just like athletic exercise and musical practice, you will see results, I promise you. And as you make progress you will feel much, much better about your current situation and your school work going forward.
